newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says can't predict N.Korea missile test.
newsitem.headline: Japan says can't predict N.Korea missile test.

text.p: Japan, worried that it could be within the firing range of North Korean missiles, said on Thursday it had no idea what the Communist state's plans were for ballistic missile tests.
"To our regret, Japan is not capable of predicting," top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
U.S. and Japanese military officials said last week that Pyongyang had made apparent preparations to test-fire a medium-range missile into the sea off Japan.
In May 1993, North Korea shocked Japan by test-firing its Rodong-1 ballistic missile into waters just off the coast of the Noto peninsula in the Sea of Japan.
A North Korean official was quoted around that time as saying Japan could be a possible target of missile attacks.
U.S. spy satellites caught the 1993 launch and tracked its trajectory, but Japan was caught off guard.
The U.S. State Department said it has several times warned Pyongyang not to conduct a missile test.
In its first official reaction to the U.S. warnings, North Korea said on Wednesday that no country had the right to interfere with another country's missile tests.

"As far as the missile firing test is concerned, it belongs to our sovereignty, and no one else is entitled or has any ground to meddle with it," a spokesman for the North Korean Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
It did not say whether North Korea was actually preparing such a test.
